question: what is a t wave abnormality?
gt_answer: T wave abnormalities are commonly seen on the electrocardiogram (EKG: tests that record heartbeat) [11728347]. They may be harmless [11728347, 32259342] or they may predict life-threatening conditions [15842426, 32975832]. Tall or prominent T-waves may be a sign of heart attack [11992348, 2301787]. Inverted T-wave (a deep in the recorded line) is linked to coronary heart disease [32975832]. Deep inverted symmetric T-waves called "cerebral T-waves" are seen in stroke patients[34239799]. Peaked T waves are the most frequent change in patients with kidney problems [31686358].

T-wave inversion is common in myocardial infarction and can be a sign of silent myocardial ischemia [22179535, 18606329, 25970951].
